column1: # WASM execute-and-diff exclusions / expected-failures manifest.
# Consumed by scripts/run_wasm_differential.sh.  Each row overrides how one
# file in the supported subset (tests/vm_parity/corpus/) is treated, so the
# gate stays green while every divergence is documented per-file — never
# silently skipped.
# Columns (TAB-separated):
#   1  file      basename WITH .esk extension
#   2  class     EXCLUDED | XFAIL
#   3  reason    one-line justification (shown in the report + ICC trace)
# EXCLUDED  the program's surface cannot run in the WASM sandbox at all (an
#           environment limitation, not a codegen correctness bug).  The
#           comparison is skipped and an EXCLUDED event is emitted.
# XFAIL     a REAL, reported WASM bug in a supported surface.  The comparison
#           still runs and is EXPECTED to diverge; a divergence is reported as
#           XFAIL (does not break the gate).  If the program ever MATCHES
#           native again (bug fixed), that XPASS FAILS the gate — the ratchet
#           that forces this row to be removed so the file becomes fully gated.
#           XFAIL never fixes the bug; it documents and tracks it.
# file
29_include_ci.esk
column3: include-ci reads a .scm file from disk; the WASM sandbox has no filesystem so the include yields () and the program prints ()() — an environment limitation, not a codegen bug. The native VM (with a filesystem) matches native codegen, so this is out-of-subset for WASM.

column1: 42_event_loop.esk
column3: ESH-0011: the program needs real file descriptors — (make-pipe) plus a kqueue/epoll/IOCP loop. The WASM sandbox has neither, so make-pipe returns #f by design and (car p) then fails on a non-pair. That is the intended fail-closed degradation, identical to make-pipe/fd-write/fd-close, not a codegen bug: the same file is byte-identical native-vs-vm-src and native-vs-vm-eskb (tests/vm_parity), and the WASM story is pinned separately by the event_loop smoke surface in scripts/check_wasm_imports.py.
